seo.title: Failed vs broken in your test report #python #testing
seo.description: Allure tracks four outcomes, not two. Failed means the check ran and said no. Broken means the test fell over first. One is your software, the other is your test.
queries: what does broken mean in allure
seo.pinned: Which one bites you more often — a failed check, or a broken test? And does your current report tell the two apart?

scenes.narration: Allure says one test failed and one broke. Those are two different problems, and most reports never tell you which.

Failed means the check ran and got the wrong answer. Your software is what is wrong. Broken means the test fell over before it ever reached the check — so the software was never even asked. Your test is what is wrong. One sends you to the app. The other sends you to the test file.

allureStage.headline: Two lanes, [two answers]
allureStage.caption: where the run stops
allureStage.premise: The left run reaches its check and is refused. The right run never gets there.

scenes.narration: And it is in the raw data, not just the picture. One grep across the result files this run wrote gives back exactly four statuses: passed, failed, broken, skipped. Four, where most people only ever count two.

recordedStep.caption: four statuses, in the files
recordedStep.premise: The result files from a real behave run.

clips.label: exactly four
clips.said:
PS allure-01> grep -ho '"status": "[a-z]*"' allure-results-bdd/*result.json | sort -u
"status": "broken"
"status": "failed"
"status": "passed"
"status": "skipped"
PS allure-01>
PS allure-01> uv run python -m behave -f allure_behave.formatter:AllureFormatter -o allure-results-bdd features
We launch ONE real Playwright/Chromium browser for the whole run and
reuse it across scenarios, closing it cleanly at the end. This is the
BDD equivalent of pytest fixtures.
"""
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
def before_all(context):
    context.playwright = sync_playwright().start()
    context.browser = context.playwright.chromium.launch()
def after_all(context):
    context.browser.close()
    context.playwright.stop()

scenes.narration: The full build is on the channel — ten checks, four outcomes, and a report written in Python with no Java anywhere.
